summary: Signed LLVM toolchain maintenance completed; existing integration acceptance failure retained for review.
changes: Upgraded clang, compiler-rt, libclc, lld, llvm, llvm-libs and llvm-lit to 23.1.3-5; installed required clang-libs dependency at the same release. Refreshed repository databases and package cache; created a read-only root recovery snapshot and private maintenance evidence. Existing ChatGPT package was current. Preserved protected configuration, repository selection, security settings, desktop session, drivers, maintenance timer and existing jobs.
tests: Before and after: package database consistency and C compile/run probes with LLD and AddressSanitizer passed. Post-update integrity checks on all eight toolchain packages reported no altered files. Final repository check reported no pending updates. Protected configuration hashes unchanged. Final package inventory review matched the approved scope. Recovery snapshot verified read-only. No GUI, game, GPU or model-backed acceptance tests performed; no production code modified.
rollback: Retained read-only root snapshot as recovery source for previous installed package files and metadata. Only the previous libclc archive was cached. No rollback executed; recovery requires inspecting actual package state and restoring the coordinated affected package set without overwriting unrelated data. Separate home, cache and log subvolumes are outside the root snapshot.
problem: A pre-existing local integration compatibility service remains failed because acceptance evidence was rejected or unavailable. Current installed identity matches the previously failed validation. Installed XFCE and LightDM also differ from recorded KDE and SDDM preferences.
solution: Completed authorized repository package maintenance. Kept the compatibility failure visible and recorded local proposals for a separate development investigation and interactive desktop reconciliation. No job resumed, acceptance baseline advanced or desktop transition performed.
reproduction: Compatibility status and installed identity were inspected read-only; existing acceptance reasons were retained. No new integration worker or model execution was launched. Desktop package inventory and display-manager selection confirmed the discrepancy.
